reference_steps.reference_observation: Axial contrast-enhanced CT of the upper abdomen at the level of the liver and porta hepatis. The liver is on the left and the spleen on the right. Contrast-enhanced venous structures are visible near the porta hepatis and mesenteric root, with areas of low attenuation suggesting intraluminal filling defects.

reference_arguments.bbox: (central upper abdomen at the porta hepatis and mesenteric venous confluence)

reference_steps.reference_observation: Low-attenuation intraluminal material is seen within the portal venous system, consistent with portal vein thrombosis. The thrombus extends into the superior mesenteric vein, indicating associated superior mesenteric vein thrombosis.

reference_arguments.query: Gpc3 knockout embryonic kidney development ureteric bud branching cystic dysplasia

reference_steps.reference_observation: Gpc3 (glypican-3) loss in mouse embryos is associated with organ overgrowth, enhanced ureteric bud branching at early stages, increased kidney size at mid-gestation, and later cystic and architectural abnormalities in the cortex and medulla.

A multi-row histology figure of embryonic mouse kidneys comparing Gpc3 +/+ (left column) and Gpc3 −/ (right column) across stages E12.0, E13.5, E16.5, and E18.5. Arrowheads highlight structures in early stages, and later panels label cortex (C), medulla (M), and cysts (Cy).

reference_arguments.attribute: compare ureteric bud branching at E12.0, kidney size at E13.5, and cortical–medullary organization and cysts at E16.5 between Gpc3 +/+ and Gpc3 -/

reference_steps.reference_observation: At E12.0, the Gpc3 −/ kidney shows more numerous and complex ureteric bud branches compared with Gpc3 +/+. At E13.5, the Gpc3 −/ kidney is noticeably larger than the control but retains broadly normal developing renal architecture. By E16.5, the Gpc3 −/ kidney shows disorganized cortical structures, reduced tubular organization in the medulla, and the presence of cystic spaces.

reference_steps.reference_answer: At E12.0, Gpc3 −/ embryos show enhanced ureteric bud branching, At E13.5, the mutant kidney is enlarged and by E16.5, the Gpc3 −/ kidney exhibits abnormal cortical organization

accepted_answers: At E12.0, Gpc3 −/ embryos show enhanced ureteric bud branching, At E13.5, the mutant kidney is enlarged and by E16.5, the Gpc3 −/ kidney exhibits abnormal cortical organization

Histology micrograph showing intestinal mucosa with crypt–villus architecture. The epithelium is composed of columnar cells, with numerous pale, mucin-filled cells interspersed. Nuclei stain dark blue to black, and mucin-rich areas stain prominently blue.

reference_arguments.query: intestinal goblet cells histology PAS Alcian blue mucin staining appearance

reference_steps.reference_observation:
1) Goblet cells are mucin-secreting epithelial cells in intestinal crypts and villi, appearing pale on routine stains.
2) Alcian blue stains acidic mucins blue; PAS stains neutral mucins magenta.
3) PAS–Alcian blue is commonly used to highlight intestinal goblet cells.
4) H&E typically shows pink cytoplasm, which is absent in mucin-rich cells.
5) Pathology atlases describe strong blue mucin staining in goblet cells with PAS–Alcian blue.

reference_steps.reference_answer: goblet cells, periodic acid–Schiff–Alcian blue stain.

accepted_answers: goblet cells, periodic acid–Schiff–Alcian blue stain.
